hub.title: AI Coding Courses and Vibe Coding | Siamese Cat Dev
hub.description: English AI coding courses from Siamese Cat Dev. Build a first app, make a game, or learn a clearer workflow for coding with AI.
hub.eyebrow: English courses by Siamese Cat Dev
hub.heading: Build with AI. Understand what you ship.
hub.lead: English courses for learners who want to build apps, games, and useful software with AI.
hub.sectionLead: Each course begins with a project and teaches the decisions behind it. Start small, then move toward more demanding software work.
hub.trialLead: Send your idea, current experience, and preferred times on WhatsApp. We will help you check the next available 30-minute trial class.
hub.trialNote: Teaching is in English. Course timing is arranged directly by WhatsApp.
hub.methodHeading: The point is not more prompts
hub.methodLead: Good AI-assisted work still needs a clear goal, a small next step, and someone willing to check the result.

method.title: Make the idea smaller
method.body: Turn a big idea into one useful result that can be built and checked.

method.title: Give AI better direction
method.body: Use examples, constraints, and clear acceptance criteria instead of hoping for a perfect prompt.

method.title: Check what changed
method.body: Learn to inspect behaviour, find mistakes, and decide what to fix next.

method.title: Keep moving toward a release
method.body: Build a habit of finishing useful slices rather than collecting unfinished demos.

faq.question: Are the courses taught in English?
faq.answer: Yes. The course content and teaching are in English. Message on WhatsApp if you want to check whether the pace is right for you.

faq.question: Do I need coding experience?
faq.answer: No coding background is required for Build Your First App with AI. The other courses are better suited to learners who already have a project or some experience with AI-assisted building.

faq.question: How do I book a trial class?
faq.answer: Use the WhatsApp button, tell us which course interests you, and send a few preferred times. We will reply with the available options.

courses.title: Build Your First App with AI
courses.metaTitle: Build Your First App with AI | Siamese Cat Dev
courses.metaDescription: A beginner English course for turning a simple idea into a working app with AI, with a free 30-minute trial class by Siamese Cat Dev.
courses.cardDescription: Start with a simple idea and learn the decisions behind a working app.
courses.heroLead: Start with a simple idea and turn it into a small app you can explain, test, and improve.
courses.heroAlt: Siamese Cat Dev character building a first app with AI
courses.outcome: A first working app and a clearer way to think about what the app is doing.
courses.promiseHeading: Make a first app you understand
courses.promise: This course is for learners who want to see how an app responds, remembers information, and follows rules. You do not need a coding background to begin.
courses.details: The work stays small on purpose. You will make decisions, ask AI for focused help, and check whether the result behaves as expected.
courses.practiceLead: The first project is a way to learn the building blocks without getting buried in technical vocabulary.

practice.title: Choose one useful idea
practice.body: Turn a broad idea into one small result that a person could actually use.

practice.title: Describe how it should behave
practice.body: Explain the inputs, decisions, and outputs before asking AI to change the app.

practice.title: Build one change at a time
practice.body: Use AI as a coding partner while keeping track of what each change is meant to do.

practice.title: Check the result
practice.body: Try the app, notice what is wrong, and use the failure to decide what to inspect next.

courses.fitHeading: This is a good place to start if
courses.fitLead: You have an idea but do not know how to turn it into something that works.
fit: You have little or no coding experience.
You want to learn by making a real, small project.
You want to understand AI-generated code instead of copying it blindly.
You are ready to explain what your app should do before building it.

faq.question: Do I need to know how to code?
faq.answer: No coding background is required for this starting course. The class focuses on making a small project and understanding the decisions behind it.

faq.question: What will I build?
faq.answer: The exact project is chosen around your starting idea. The goal is a small working app that you can explain, test, and continue improving.

courses.title: Make a Game with AI
courses.metaTitle: Make a Game with AI | Siamese Cat Dev
courses.metaDescription: Learn to turn a game idea into a playable project with AI. Explore rules, characters, levels, testing, and iteration in English.
courses.cardDescription: Design the rules, characters, and levels that turn an idea into a playable project.
courses.heroLead: Turn game ideas into a playable project by working through rules, characters, levels, and the loop that keeps a game moving.
courses.heroAlt: Siamese Cat Dev character designing a game with AI
courses.outcome: A playable game concept with rules you can explain and decisions you can improve.
courses.promise: A game is more than a character on a screen. It needs a clear loop: what the player does, what changes, and what counts as progress.
courses.details: AI can help with parts of the build, but you still need to decide how the game should feel and how to tell whether it is working.
courses.practiceLead: Build the idea from the player's point of view, then test the parts that make the project feel like a game.

practice.title: Define the game loop
practice.body: Describe the repeatable action that gives the player a reason to continue.

practice.title: Design the rules
practice.body: Decide what can happen, what cannot happen, and what changes when the player acts.

practice.title: Shape a playable level
practice.body: Use characters, obstacles, goals, and feedback to give the player a clear next move.

practice.title: Test and revise
practice.body: Play the project, find the confusing or broken parts, and make one focused improvement at a time.

courses.fitHeading: This is a good place to start if
courses.fitLead: You have a game idea and want to understand how an idea becomes a playable system.
fit: You enjoy games and want to explore how they are made.
You want a project with visible rules and immediate feedback.
You are ready to test your idea instead of only describing it.
You want to use AI without handing over every design decision.

faq.question: Do I need to be a game designer?
faq.answer: No. You can start with a simple game idea. The course helps you turn that idea into rules, player actions, and a small playable project.

faq.question: Will the course use a specific game engine?
faq.answer: The right starting tool depends on the project and your current experience. Use the trial conversation to describe your idea before choosing a tool.

courses.title: Coding with AI for Real Applications
courses.metaTitle: Coding with AI | Plan, Build and Deploy | Siamese Cat Dev
courses.metaDescription: Move beyond quick demos with an English vibe coding course about planning, designing, building, checking, and deploying applications with AI.
courses.cardDescription: Move from quick demos to a workflow for planning, checking, and deploying software.
courses.heroLead: Move beyond a quick demo. Learn a practical workflow to plan, design, build, and deploy software with AI.
courses.heroAlt: Siamese Cat Dev character working through an AI-assisted software workflow
courses.outcome: A repeatable plan for taking an AI-assisted project from idea to a more reliable release.
courses.promise: This course is for learners who have used AI to make prototypes and want a more dependable way to work.
courses.details: You will look at the decisions around architecture, data, debugging, security, and deployment. The aim is not more prompts. It is better control over the system you are building.
courses.practiceLead: A useful AI workflow has a shape. It starts with a decision, creates a small change, and ends with a check.

practice.title: Plan the system
practice.body: Break the product into a clear first release and identify the parts that need to work together.

practice.title: Design the boundaries
practice.body: Make sensible decisions about data, users, permissions, and what the first version should not do.

practice.title: Guide the build
practice.body: Give an AI coding agent useful context, examples, and checks so its changes remain understandable.

practice.title: Verify before release
practice.body: Use tests, manual checks, security questions, and deployment habits that expose problems before users do.

courses.fitHeading: This is a good place to start if
courses.fitLead: You can make a prototype but want a clearer path to software that other people can use.
fit: You have already tried vibe coding or AI-assisted development.
You want to understand architecture, data, debugging, and deployment.
You are willing to inspect and test what AI creates.
You want a process that scales better than copying one prompt after another.

faq.question: Is this course for complete beginners?
faq.answer: It is better suited to learners who have already made a prototype or understand the basic idea of building with AI. Start with the first app course if you are new to the workflow.

faq.question: Does this course teach one specific AI tool?
faq.answer: The focus is the workflow and the engineering decisions, not a temporary list of tools. The best tools to use depend on the project you bring.
